drafts.title: $1,350 cabin heater, the day the warranty ended (Sun ~2 PM)
drafts.angle: Calm owner-to-owner winter prep. Know your dates. Not a scare post and not anti-Tesla.
bullets: A 2018 Model 3 owner in Canada says the car quit on the exact day its 8-year battery warranty expired; repair estimate $3,825.98.
The cause looked like the cabin heater (PTC heater), about $1,350 installed; another owner paid $2,100 for the same part.
The battery warranty is separate from the basic warranty, so the timing alone doesn't mean it would have been covered.
Tesla's own cold-weather advice: precondition while plugged in, and expect less range in the cold (outside guides say about 15% to 30%).
drafts.body:
$1,350. That's one Tesla owner's cabin heater bill, and it died the day his battery warranty ran out.

My warranty ends [___]. Before winter I'm [checking the dates in the app / looking at whether an extended plan is worth it for me]. The battery warranty and the basic warranty are different clocks, so the date alone doesn't tell the whole story.

Tesla's own tip still holds: precondition while you're plugged in, and expect less range when it's cold. I'm not trying to scare anybody. I just want to know my dates before the first hard freeze.

Do you know when yours runs out?
drafts.ocr_why: Real dollar, practical takeaway, owner-to-owner tone. Keep the rewrite calm.
